text:
Marathon Petroleum fell slightly today despite a strong two-week run, as oil prices retreated from their recent peaks. Brent crude, which had climbed above $109 following Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities earlier this week, has pulled back to around $126 globally and $102 domestically—the kind of modest pullback that can weigh on refiner stocks even when prices remain elevated. The company also faces a headwind from refineries already running near capacity (93.5%), which limits how much additional throughput can boost profits from higher crude costs.

The broader geopolitical tension that drove oil higher this week—Iranian threats, Houthi missile strikes, and attacks on Russian and Saudi energy infrastructure—appears to have stabilized rather than escalated further, taking some of the urgency out of the market. With refineries operating close to maximum and crude inventories at 698 million barrels (a healthy level), the conditions that powered Marathon's 9% gain over two weeks have plateaued.
